title: Presente de Subjuntivo — Practice
description: Authored B1 practice set for forming the present subjunctive: the opposite-vowel endings built off the yo form, stem and spelling changes, and the six fully irregular verbs.

lessons.summary: To form the present subjunctive, start from the 'yo' form of the present indicative, drop the -o, and add the opposite vowel endings: -ar verbs take -e, -es, -e, -emos, -en (hablo → hable, hables, hable, hablemos, hablen) and -er/-ir verbs take -a, -as, -a, -amos, -an (como → coma; vivo → viva). Because it is built off the yo form, any irregularity there carries through every person: tengo → tenga, hago → haga, digo → diga, pongo → ponga, salgo → salga, vengo → venga, conozco → conozca, veo → vea, traigo → traiga, oigo → oiga. Boot verbs keep their stem change everywhere except nosotros (poder → pueda but podamos; querer → quiera but queramos); -ir boot verbs also change in nosotros (dormir → durmamos, pedir → pidamos). Verbs in -car/-gar/-zar shift spelling to keep the sound: buscar → busque, llegar → llegue, empezar → empiece. Six verbs are simply irregular: ser → sea, ir → vaya, saber → sepa, haber → haya, estar → esté, dar → dé. Which expressions require the subjunctive is a separate topic (Subjunctive Triggers) — here the job is producing the form.

examples.english: I want you to come with me.

examples.spanish: Es importante que digas la verdad.
examples.english: It's important that you tell the truth.

examples.spanish: Te lo digo para que lo sepas.
examples.english: I'm telling you so that you know.

items.explanation: -ar verbs take the -e endings: hablo → hable.
hablo → hables.
-er/-ir verbs take the -a endings: como → coma.
vivo → vivamos.
hablo → hablen.
Built off the yo form: tengo → tenga.
hago → haga.
digo → digan. The yo-form irregularity carries through every person.
salgo → salgas.
conozco → conozca.
ser is one of the six fully irregular verbs: sea, seas, sea, seamos, sean.
ir → vaya, vayas, vaya, vayamos, vayan.
saber → sepa, sepas, sepa, sepamos, sepan.
estar keeps a written accent: esté, estés, esté, estemos, estén.
dar → dé, des, dé, demos, den. The accent on 'dé' separates it from the preposition 'de'.

items.prompt: Present subjunctive of impersonal 'hay' ('that there be'): ___
items.explanation: haber → haya. 'No creo que haya tiempo.'
Boot verb: puedo → pueda. Nosotros loses the change: podamos.
quiero → quieras. Nosotros: queramos.
-ir boot verbs also change in nosotros — o → u: durmamos (not 'dormamos').
-car verbs shift to -qu- to keep the hard sound: busque.
-gar verbs add a u: llegues.

items.promptEnglish: I want you to come with me.
items.explanation: vengo → vengas.

items.promptEnglish: It's important that you tell the truth.
items.explanation: digo → digas.
Boot verb, third person only: llueve → llueva.
estar is irregular and accented: estés.

items.prompt: Te lo digo para que lo ___. (saber, tú)
items.promptEnglish: I'm telling you so that you know.
items.explanation: saber → sepas.
Impersonal haber in the subjunctive: haya.

items.prompt: Antes de que ___, cierra la puerta. (salir, nosotros)
items.promptEnglish: Before we leave, close the door.
items.explanation: salgo → salgamos.

items.promptEnglish: I want you to come now.
items.explanation: 'Querer que' takes the subjunctive, so the form is vengas, not the indicative vienes.

items.promptEnglish: It's better that we sleep early.
items.explanation: -ir boot verbs go o → u in nosotros: durmamos.

items.prompt: Into the present subjunctive: "Ella habla español" → "Quiero que ella ___ español."
items.promptEnglish: I want her to speak Spanish.
items.explanation: habla → hable (the -ar verb takes the -e ending).

items.prompt: Into the present subjunctive: "Vas al médico" → "Es necesario que ___ al médico."
items.promptEnglish: It's necessary that you go to the doctor.
items.explanation: ir is irregular: vas → vayas.

items.prompt: Escribe una frase que empiece con "Espero que…" usando el presente de subjuntivo.
items.promptEnglish: Write a sentence starting with "Espero que…" using the present subjunctive.
items.guidance: Must be grammatical Spanish where the verb after 'Espero que' is in the present subjunctive (e.g. 'Espero que tengas un buen día', 'Espero que puedas venir'). Mark incorrect if the verb is in the indicative ('Espero que tienes…'), or if the subjunctive form itself is misconjugated.
items.sampleAnswer: Espero que tengas un buen día.
items.explanation: 'Esperar que' requires the subjunctive — build the form off the yo form with the opposite vowel.
